title: At someone's home
goal: Be a good guest (and host) in a Nepali home: ask what's OK, accept and decline food and drink gracefully, help with chores, stay the night, and talk about how things used to be.
intro:
Sooner or later a Nepali friend will say **घरमा आऊ न** 'come over'. Visiting a home is where Nepali politeness is most alive: the host insists, the guest declines, the host insists again — and there are a few quiet rules about shoes, the kitchen and food that's been touched (जुठो).

In this unit you'll learn to ask **'should I…? / is it OK to…?'** (जुत्ता खोल्नुपर्छ? भान्सामा जान हुन्छ?), to handle offers like a local (**चिया खानुहुन्न?** — **भइहाल्छ, धन्यवाद**), and the **habitual past** for 'used to': म सानो छँदा यहीँ **बस्थेँ** 'I used to live right here when I was little' — the tense of family stories over tea.

vocab.note: भुइँमा बस्नु 'to sit on the floor'. भुइँ तला 'ground floor'.
Homes keep a pile of house chappals by the door for guests.
f. पूजा गर्नु 'to do puja'; पूजा कोठा 'prayer room'.
घरको नियम 'house rule'.
एक गिलास पानी 'a glass of water'.
Also प्लेट. Dal bhat is eaten from a थाल.
Many Nepalis eat dal bhat with their right hand; guests are usually offered a spoon.

vocab.en: touched by someone's mouth or eaten from (so not to be shared); used, dirty (dishes)
vocab.note: A key idea in Nepali homes: food or a glass you have eaten/drunk from is जुठो and is not offered to others. जुठो पार्नु 'to make जुठो'.
The opposite of जुठो: food kept apart for the gods or the family before anyone eats.

vocab.en: to help out, give a hand
vocab.note: Homely and colloquial — the word for helping with chores. मद्दत गर्नु is more general.
भुइँ पुछ्नु 'to mop the floor', आँसु पुछ्नु 'to wipe away tears'.
The soft grass broom found in every Nepali home.
फोहोर फाल्नु 'to throw out the rubbish'.
मेरो पालो 'my turn'; पालैपालो 'taking turns'.
Causative of सुक्नु 'to dry (by itself)': लुगा सुक्यो 'the washing is dry'.
The open space in front of or inside a house, where people sit in the sun and dry washing.
बास बस्नु 'to stay the night'.
यता + ऐ '(right) here'. Also उतै 'right there'.
The made-up bed (mattress, sheet, quilt); खाट is the frame.
Thick cotton quilt — essential in winter, since houses have no heating.
Colloquial. More neutral: त्यतिबेला 'at that time'.
Past हुर्केँ, हुर्क्यो. Causative हुर्काउनु 'to bring up (a child)'.
f. X-को सम्झना आयो '(it) reminded me of X / I thought of X'.

phrases.en: Come in — make yourself at home.
phrases.note: Lit. 'think of it as your own home'.

phrases.en: Where shall I put my shoes?
Is it OK to go into the kitchen?
phrases.note: In traditional homes the kitchen is a semi-sacred space — always ask.

phrases.en: Won't you have something (to eat or drink)?
I'm fine, thanks — don't go to any trouble.
phrases.note: भइहाल्छ 'it's fine as it is' — the softest way to decline.

phrases.en: What time are we getting up tomorrow?
I used to live right here when I was little.
phrases.note: छँदा 'while (I) was' — the -दा form of छ.

phrases.en: Those were the days! (lit. how fun it was back then)
I'll be off now, it's getting late.
phrases.note: हिँड्नु 'walk' is the everyday word for 'set off, leave'.

grammar.title: Used to: the habitual past -थ्यो
grammar.body:
For things that **used to happen** regularly, Nepali has its own tense: the habitual past. Take the present habitual (गर्छ) and swap छ for **थ्यो**:

म **गर्थेँ** *gartheṃ* · हामी **गर्थ्यौँ** *garthyauṃ*
तिमी **गर्थ्यौ** *garthyau* · ऊ **गर्थ्यो** *garthyo* (f **गर्थी** *garthi*)
उनीहरू **गर्थे** *garthe* · तपाईं/उहाँ **गर्नुहुन्थ्यो** *garnuhunthyo*

Vowel stems keep their nasal: खानु → **खान्थेँ, खान्थ्यो**; जानु → **जान्थेँ, जान्थ्यो**; आउनु → **आउँथेँ, आउँथ्यो**; हुनु → **हुन्थ्यो**.

**Negative**: put the present negative before थ्यो: म **गर्दिनथेँ**, ऊ **गर्दैनथ्यो**, उनीहरू **गर्दैनथे**; म **खाँदिनथेँ** 'I didn't use to eat'.

It pairs naturally with **सानो छँदा / सानो हुँदा** 'when I was little', **पहिले** 'before', **उतिबेला** 'back then'.

**Don't confuse** it with the simple past: म पोखरा **गएँ** 'I went to Pokhara (once)' vs म पोखरा **जान्थेँ** 'I used to go to Pokhara'. And not with **थियो** alone, which is just 'was'.

**Bonus — wishes**: X **भए हुन्थ्यो** 'it would be nice (to have) X', literally 'if there were X, it would be': एक कप चिया **भए हुन्थ्यो** 'a cup of tea would be nice'. Polite and very common.

examples.en: When I was little I used to sleep next to Grandma.
We used to go to my uncle's (mother's family home) every monsoon.

examples.native: बुबा पहिले चुरोट खानुहुन्थ्यो, अहिले छोड्नुभयो।
examples.roman: bubā pahile churoṭ khānuhunthyo, ahile chhoḍnubhayo.
examples.en: Dad used to smoke, but he's given up now.
There used to be lots of power cuts here.
Back then I didn't use to drink tea.
A cup of tea would be nice.

grammar.title: Offering, insisting and declining like a local
grammar.body:
Unit 18 gave you the basics (लिनुहोस् न, पुग्यो, अलिकति मात्र). Three more tools make you sound at home:

**1. The negative-question offer.** Hosts rarely say 'do you want tea?' — they say **'won't you have tea?'**: चिया **खानुहुन्न**? (तपाईं) · चिया **खाँदैनौ**? (तिमी). It's gentle and leaves room for the ritual first 'no'. Answer **हुन्छ** to accept.

**2. -इहाल्नु 'just, right away, go ahead and'** (unit 23). Hosts use it all the time to make an offer sound quick and no-fuss: म चिया **बनाइहाल्छु** 'I'll just make some tea', **लिइहाल्नुहोस्** 'go on, take it', **खाइहाल** 'go on, eat' (to a friend). Hosts use it to brush aside your protests.

**3. Declining softly.** **भइहाल्छ** (lit. 'it's already fine') = 'no need, don't bother'. Give a reason rather than a bare no: **पर्दैन, भर्खर खाएर आएँ** 'no need, I've just eaten'. A flat **होइन** or **चाहिँदैन** sounds cold.

**The dance**: the host offers, you decline once (भइहाल्छ), the host insists (लिइहाल्नुहोस् न!), and you accept a little (**ल, अलिकति मात्र**). Declining twice firmly is fine for a second helping — not for the first cup of tea.

examples.en: Won't you have a little rice?
Sit down, I'll just make some tea.
Go on, take some — don't be shy.
Well, since you insist, I'll have a little.

grammar.title: Should I…? Is it OK to…?
grammar.body:
Four ways to check what's expected in someone's home:

**-ऊँ?** 'shall I?' (from unit 18) — an offer or a request for instructions: जुत्ता कहाँ **राखूँ**? 'where shall I put my shoes?' · म **सघाऊँ**? 'shall I help?'

**-ने?** 'what's the plan / what do we do?' — impersonal, asks about the arrangement or custom: भोलि कति बजे **उठ्ने**? 'what time are we getting up?' · के **लगाउने**? 'what should I wear?' · फोहोर कहाँ **फाल्ने**? 'where does the rubbish go?'

**-नुपर्छ?** 'do I have to?': जुत्ता **खोल्नुपर्छ**? 'do I need to take my shoes off?' The relaxed answer is **पर्दैन** 'no need'.

**-न हुन्छ?** 'is it OK / allowed to…?' (custom and permission): भान्सामा **जान हुन्छ**? · यहाँ **बस्न हुन्छ**? Answer **हुन्छ** 'yes, fine' or **हुँदैन** 'no'. For a firm rule people say **-नुहुँदैन** 'one mustn't' (unit 9): पूजा कोठामा जुत्ता लगाएर **जानुहुँदैन**.

**The trap**: **-न हुन्छ** (permission, 'is it OK to') and **-नुहुन्छ** (the polite 'you do') look alike. जान हुन्छ? 'is it OK to go?' vs जानुहुन्छ? 'are you going?'

examples.en: Is it OK to come in wearing slippers?
What should I bring? Sweets or fruit?
Shall I sleep in this room?
Do I need to bring my own towel?
You mustn't touch the pots with a hand you've eaten with.

dialogue.title: A night at Anjali's in Pokhara
dialogue.setting: Sarah visits her friend Anjali's family home in Pokhara. Anjali's mother treats her like a daughter and uses तिमी with her; Sarah calls her आन्टी.

lines.speaker: Anjali
lines.en: You made it? Come in, come in!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Namaste, auntie! Where shall I put my shoes?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: त्यहीँ ढोकाछेउ राख, नानी। यो चप्पल लगाऊ, आफ्नै घर सम्झ है।
lines.roman: tyahiṃ ḍhokāchheu rākha, nāni. yo chappal lagāu, āphnai ghar samjha hai.
lines.en: Just leave them by the door, dear. Put these slippers on, and make yourself at home.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.en: Won't you have something? I'll just make some tea.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: भइहाल्छ आन्टी, भर्खर खाना खाएर आएँ।
lines.roman: bhaihālchha ānṭi, bharkhar khānā khāera āeṃ.
lines.en: I'm fine, auntie — I've just eaten.

lines.speaker: Anjali
lines.native: खाना नखाए पनि चिया त खानैपर्छ, यो घरको नियम हो!
lines.roman: khānā nakhāe pani chiyā ta khānaiparchha, yo gharko niyam ho!
lines.en: Even if you don't eat, you HAVE to have tea — house rule!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: ल ठीक छ, चिया मात्र। म केही सघाऊँ?
lines.roman: la ṭhik chha, chiyā mātra. ma kehi saghāuṃ?
lines.en: OK, OK — just tea. Can I help with anything?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: पर्दैन, तिमी त पाहुना हौ! बस, गफ गर।
lines.roman: pardaina, timi ta pāhunā hau! basa, gaph gara.
lines.en: No need, you're the guest! Sit down and chat.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: यो घर त कति राम्रो! अञ्जली, तिमी यहीँ हुर्क्यौ?
lines.roman: yo ghar ta kati rāmro! Añjali, timi yahiṃ hurkyau?
lines.en: What a lovely house! Anjali, did you grow up here?

lines.speaker: Anjali
lines.native: हो, म सानो छँदा दसैंमा यही आँगनमा दिनभरि चङ्गा उडाउँथेँ।
lines.roman: ho, ma sāno chhaṃdā dasaiṃmā yahi āṃganmā dinbhari chaṅgā uḍāuṃtheṃ.
lines.en: Yes — when I was little I used to fly kites in this very courtyard all day at Dashain.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: अनि बेलुका पढ्न भन्यो भने सुत्थी!
lines.roman: ani belukā paḍhna bhanyo bhane sutthi!
lines.en: And in the evening, if you told her to study, she'd fall asleep!

lines.speaker: Anjali
lines.en: Mum! Why are you telling her that?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: ल, आज यतै बास बस, नानी। राति बाटो राम्रो छैन।
lines.roman: la, āja yatai bās basa, nāni. rāti bāṭo rāmro chhaina.
lines.en: Right — stay the night here, dear. The road's not good at night.

culture:
**Shoes off** at the door, always; you'll be handed house चप्पल. The **kitchen** (भान्सा) and the **puja room** are the most sacred parts of a traditional home — ask before going in, and never with shoes. The idea of **जुठो** runs through Nepali eating: once food or a glass has touched your lips it's जुठो, so you don't offer someone a bite of your food, dip your own spoon into a shared dish, or drink from someone else's bottle — people pour water into their mouths from above without touching the rim. Eat and pass things with your **right hand**.

Bring a small **कोसेली** (fruit, sweets, biscuits). Expect tea within minutes of arriving; declining once with **भइहाल्छ** is polite, refusing outright isn't. Hosts will refuse your offers to help with the dishes — offering is still appreciated, and with friends your own age you can just do it.

In cities, young people call a friend's parents **आन्टी / अंकल**; in more traditional homes **आमा / बुबा** (or दिदी/दाइ for younger parents). An older woman will often call you **नानी** (to a girl) or **बाबु** (to a boy) and use तिमी — that's warmth, not rudeness.

tip.title: Shall I…? Do I have to…? Is it OK to…?
tip.body:
- **-ऊँ?** 'shall I?': जुत्ता कहाँ **राखूँ**?
- **-नुपर्छ?** 'do I have to?': जुत्ता **खोल्नुपर्छ**?
- **-न हुन्छ?** 'is it OK to?': भान्सामा **जान हुन्छ**? — firm 'no': **-नुहुँदैन**.
- Careful: जान हुन्छ? 'is it OK to go?' ≠ जानुहुन्छ? 'are you going?'

sentences.en: Shall I put my bag here?
Do I need to take my shoes off inside?

sentences.native: भुइँ चिसो छ, यो चप्पल लगाउनुहोस्।
sentences.roman: bhuiṃ chiso chha, yo chappal lagāunuhos.
sentences.en: The floor's cold — put these slippers on.
Is it OK to sit on the sofa?
You mustn't go into the prayer room with your shoes on.
What time do I have to be back home by at night?

sentences.native: आमाको एउटै नियम छ: खाना खाँदा फोन नचलाउनू!
sentences.roman: āmāko euṭai niyam chha: khānā khāṃdā phon nachalāunu!
sentences.en: Mum has one rule: no phones while you're eating!
Is it OK to take photos or not?

sentences.native: बिहान पूजा गर्दा हल्ला नगर्नू है।
sentences.roman: bihāna pujā gardā hallā nagarnu hai.
sentences.en: Don't make any noise during the morning puja, OK?
Shall I sit here?

tip.title: Offers and soft refusals
tip.body:
- Hosts offer with a **negative question**: चिया **खानुहुन्न**? (to a friend: **खाँदैनौ**?)
- **-इहाल्नु** = 'just / go ahead': म **बनाइहाल्छु** 'I'll just make it', **लिइहाल्नुहोस्** 'go on, take it'.
- Decline softly: **भइहाल्छ** 'I'm fine' + a reason — not a flat होइन.

sentences.en: Won't you have a little tea?
Won't you have a glass of water? (to a friend)
Sit a sec, I'll just serve the food.

sentences.native: तपाईंको थाल त खाली भयो, अलिकति दाल थपूँ?
sentences.roman: tapāiṃko thāl ta khāli bhayo, alikati dāl thapuṃ?
sentences.en: Your plate's empty — shall I add a bit more dal?
I'm fine, really — I'm full.

sentences.native: ल ठीक छ, आधा गिलास मात्र।
sentences.roman: la ṭhik chha, ādhā gilās mātra.
sentences.en: OK then, just half a glass.
Just put the leftover curry in a bowl.
Don't put a spoon you've eaten with into the pot, OK?

sentences.native: यो गिलास जुठो हो, अर्को लिनुहोस्।
sentences.roman: yo gilās juṭho ho, arko linuhos.
sentences.en: This glass has been used — take another one.

sentences.native: आमा पहिले भगवानलाई चोखो भात चढाउनुहुन्छ।
sentences.roman: āmā pahile bhagawānlāi chokho bhāt chaḍhāunuhunchha.
sentences.en: Mum first offers untouched rice to the gods.
Won't you take anything? At least have a little!

tip.title: Offering to help
tip.body:
- **सघाउनु** is the homely word for helping out: म **सघाऊँ**?
- Offer a specific job with **-इदिऊँ?** 'shall I … for you?': भाँडा **माझिदिऊँ**?
- Say what you'll do with **-इदिन्छु**: म कोठा **बढारिदिन्छु**.
- Turns: आज **मेरो पालो** 'it's my turn today'.

sentences.en: Shall I do the dishes for you?

sentences.native: आज भाँडा माझ्ने पालो कसको हो?
sentences.roman: āja bhāṃḍā mājhne pālo kasko ho?
sentences.en: Whose turn is it to do the dishes today?

sentences.native: आज मेरो पालो, तिमी आराम गर।
sentences.roman: āja mero pālo, timi ārām gara.
sentences.en: It's my turn today — you have a rest.
I'll sweep the room.
Where's the broom?
Shall I wipe the table?
Where does the rubbish go?
Shall I hang the washing out to dry in the yard?

sentences.native: पर्दैन, तिमी बस, म आफैँ गर्छु।
sentences.roman: pardaina, timi basa, ma āphaiṃ garchhu.
sentences.en: No need — you sit, I'll do it myself.
Thanks for helping out.
Apparently you're not supposed to let a guest do any work!

tip.title: What's the plan? -ने?
tip.body:
- **-ने?** asks about the plan or the custom, with no 'I' or 'you' in the verb: भोलि के **खाने**? 'what shall we have tomorrow?', कुन कोठामा **सुत्ने**? 'which room am I sleeping in?'
- **-नुपर्छ?** 'do I have to?': म भोलि कति बजे **हिँड्नुपर्छ**?
- **-न मिल्छ?** 'would it be possible?': बास **बस्न मिल्छ**?

sentences.en: So I'm sleeping here tonight?
Which room am I sleeping in?
It's cold — shall I get you another quilt?
I've put a fresh sheet on the bed for you.
Do I need to bring a towel and soap?
When does the hot water come on for a shower?
What shall we have tomorrow morning?

sentences.native: आज यतै बस, राति बस छैन।
sentences.roman: āja yatai basa, rāti bas chhaina.
sentences.en: Stay here tonight — there's no bus at night.
Could I stay the night at your place?
What time do I need to leave tomorrow?

tip.title: Used to: -थ्यो
tip.body:
- Present habitual with **थ्यो** instead of छ: म गर्**थेँ**, ऊ गर्**थ्यो**, हामी गर्**थ्यौँ**, तपाईं गर्नुहुन्**थ्यो**.
- Vowel stems: जा**न्थेँ**, खा**न्थ्यो**, आउँ**थ्यो**.
- Negative: म गर्**दिनथेँ**, ऊ गर्**दैनथ्यो**.
- Not the one-off past: म गएँ 'I went' vs म जान्थेँ 'I used to go'.

sentences.native: हामी सानो छँदा हरेक दसैंमा गाउँ जान्थ्यौँ।
sentences.roman: hāmi sāno chhaṃdā harek dasaiṃmā gāuṃ jānthyauṃ.
sentences.en: When we were little we used to go to the village every Dashain.

sentences.native: म यही घरमा हुर्केँ, यहीँ खेल्थेँ।
sentences.roman: ma yahi gharmā hurkeṃ, yahiṃ kheltheṃ.
sentences.en: I grew up in this very house — I used to play right here.
You used to be able to see the mountains from here.
Grandma used to tell us stories at night.

sentences.native: उतिबेला मोबाइल थिएन, हामी बाहिर खेल्थ्यौँ।
sentences.roman: utibelā mobāil thiena, hāmi bāhira khelthyauṃ.
sentences.en: Back then there were no mobiles — we used to play outside.
What were you like as a kid?

sentences.native: म पहिले मासु खाँदिनथेँ, अहिले खान्छु।
sentences.roman: ma pahile māsu khāṃdinatheṃ, ahile khānchhu.
sentences.en: I didn't use to eat meat — now I do.

sentences.native: बुबा दिनहुँ बिहान हिँडेर अफिस जानुहुन्थ्यो।
sentences.roman: bubā dinahuṃ bihāna hiṃḍera aphis jānuhunthyo.
sentences.en: Dad used to walk to the office every morning.

sentences.native: यो फोटो हेर्दा धेरै कुराको सम्झना आयो।
sentences.roman: yo phoṭo herdā dherai kurāko samjhanā āyo.
sentences.en: Looking at this photo brings back lots of memories.

sentences.native: उतिबेला यहाँ यति धेरै घर थिएनन्।
sentences.roman: utibelā yahāṃ yati dherai ghar thienan.
sentences.en: Back then there weren't this many houses here.
A hot cup of tea would be nice right now!
